subject: Embedding dimensionality & drift — qualification & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Embedding dimensionality & drift — qualification & next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier, Elena / Jordan — good conversation. High-level recap + next steps so we don’t lose momentum. Short TL;DR up top, then details.

TL;DR
- Preliminary eval on your sample data shows strong semantic clustering with a 1536-d embedding baseline (candidate models below).
- Two open concerns before pilot: (1) dimensionality mismatch between some legacy vectors and our candidate embeddings, (2) short-term drift in query distribution for one metadata-heavy vertical.
- Proposed next steps: canonical prompt set + 48-hour drift-run, small holdout production validation, and a 30-minute follow-up to lock pilot scope.

What we ran (very brief)
- Dataset: 8k representative documents + 1k query prompts from the set you shared (thanks for the CSV).
- Models evaluated: redwood/embed-large-v2 (1536d), open/embed-768-lite (768d), and a quantized variant redwood/embed-large-v2-q4_0 (1536d).
- Metrics: MRR@10, NDCG@10, and semantic recall @ 0.75 cosine threshold.
- Result highlight: redwood/embed-large-v2 gave NDCG@10 = 0.72, MRR@10 = 0.48; open/embed-768-lite gave NDCG@10 = 0.63, MRR@10 = 0.39.

What we recommend now (short list)
- Primary candidate: redwood/embed-large-v2 (1536 dims) — best retrieval quality on your knowledge graph-heavy docs.
- Fallback (lower cost): open/embed-768-lite — smaller dims reduce index size and memory pressure, with modest quality reduction.
- Quantized variant: redwood/embed-large-v2-q4_0 for Dedicated/Private if you want cost savings with minimal quality impact in most queries.

Drift & dimensionality notes
- We observed a higher variance in vector norms for clinical-protocol documents vs marketing content; this suggests per-vertical normalization or per-collection PCA may help.
- Some of your legacy embeddings are 1024d. Mixing 1024d and 1536d in a single nearest-neighbor index will bias distance calculations; we recommend either re-embedding the legacy corpus or maintaining a separate index + cross-index routing.

Next steps (please confirm):
1) You provide a ~2k item holdout (ideally from the last 30 days) — we run a 48-hour drift simulation and a short recall sweep.
2) We share the canonical prompt set and evaluation harness (CSV + benchmark scripts) — you can run locally or we run in a sandbox.
3) Book a 30-minute sync next week to review pilot scope and SLAs.

Attachments: nexport_semsearch_sample_prompts.csv (prompt set we used), nexport-eval-results-20270411.csv (full eval export).

Open questions for you (quick):
- Is re-embedding the legacy 1024d corpus a hard constraint?
- Any maximum index RAM per replica we should plan for?
- Compliance: will this pilot require our Private deployment and encrypted vectors?

Suggested times to sync (PT): Wed 04/14 10:00–10:30 or Thu 04/15 09:00–09:30. I’ll drop a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Re-embedding: re-embedding all historic docs is not impossible but costly. Our preference is to avoid wholesale re-embeds initially; hence the separate-index idea is appealing.

2) Index RAM: our current infra target is <= 12GB per replica for customer search nodes. Can you provide expected RAM for the redwood/embed-large-v2 baseline for a 1M vector index (approx)?

3) Compliance: we likely need encrypted-at-rest vectors and audit logs; I’ll confirm with security but plan for Private deployment as a possibility.

We can do Wed 04/14 10:00 PT. Please book.

—Elena

Nice notes — a couple of implementation bullets from the eval team: 

- RAM estimate: redwood/embed-large-v2 (1536d float32) ~ 6 bytes per dim after optimized storage using our packing (approx 9KB/vector when accounting for index overhead). For 1M vectors expect ~9–12GB per replica depending on index configuration. Quantized (q4_0) drops that by ~40–60%.
- Canonical eval: we’ll share a small harness (Python + SQL) that computes MRR/NDCG and a per-query recall curve. Link: https://redwood.ai/drive/Shared/benchmarks/nexport-embed-20270411
- Prompt set & snippet: moving the sample prompts to a shared Gist (see related_links) so you can review exact query wording.

On the drift side: we propose a 48-hour synthetic drift-run where we replay the last 30 days at scaled velocity and compute drift signal: mean cosine shift, per-namespace centroid drift, and PCA-based eigenvalue shifts. If the mean cosine shift exceeds 0.06 we flag an alert and recommend incremental re-index or online re-embedding.

Happy to take point on running the drift-run once we have the holdout.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — looping in from security. Short answers to the sandbox / PII questions: 

- Redaction: yes — we can apply configurable PII redaction before embeddings are generated in the Hosted sandbox. We'll run a PII tokenization pass and replace tokens with stable hashes prior to vectorizing. We’ll document the transform in the submission README.
- Encrypted vectors: for Private deployments we support envelope-encrypted vectors (KMS/HSM integrations) and audit logs for vector access.
- Pilot data retention: Hosted sandbox results retained for 30 days by default; Private deployments can have custom retention windows.

Attached: nexport_security_questionnaire_answers.pdf (answers to your initial SOC/Security checklist). If you need anything else before Wed’s call ping me and I’ll prep details.
